member.name: T:SysWeaver.CommandLine
member.summary:
Command line parser and help (syntax) generator.
An instance is the result of a parse: the positional and the that were found.
Options can be declared explicitly () or generated from the public members of an options object (), in which case the XML documentation summary of each member (via SysWeaver.Docs) becomes its help text.
member.remarks: The static formatting fields (prefixes, tags, comparer) are global mutable settings shared by the whole process; change them once at startup.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.CommandLine.GetOptions(System.Object,SysWeaver.CommandLine.OptionMembers)
member.summary: Generates command line options from the public instance members of an object, each paired with a setter that assigns the parsed value.
member.param: The object whose members define the options; its current member values become the displayed defaults.
Which members to include.
member.returns: The help options (, , with null setters) followed by one option per supported member. The setter takes (instance, value).

remarks.para: Option names are the member names. Members whose type has no parser are treated as nested option objects (created with the default constructor if null) and their members are exposed as "Member.SubMember". An object created for a null member is only used to find the options, it is not assigned to , so the setter of such a nested option throws a . A nested member whose type is already on the current nesting path (ex: Node.Child of type Node) is skipped, so self-referencing types don't recurse.

A struct typed nested member must be a field: a struct typed property (without a parser) is skipped, it has no options (a property returns a copy of the struct, so its members can't be assigned through it). Using such an option ("-StructProp.Member") throws the of an unknown option.
Indexers and properties without a getter are skipped, so are read-only fields and properties without a setter unless they are nested option objects.
A boolean member that is currently false becomes a flag option (no value, sets it to true); other members take a single "value" argument.
The help text is the member's XML documentation summary. Setters are compiled expressions, so this is relatively expensive; the result is lazily enumerated and not cached.

member.remarks:
The command line is "[options] SourceFiles [DestFolder]", where options are generated from the public members of the options type (see ).
The processing methods return a process exit code (to return from Main) following the common convention 0 = success, non-zero (1-255) = failure: 0 = success (also when help was requested with "-?" or "-help"), 1 = processing threw an exception, 2 = invalid command line (or the validation threw), else the first non-zero value returned by the validation or file callback (passed through unchanged, so return values in 1-255 from them: Linux truncates exit codes to 8 bits and Windows "if errorlevel 1" ignores negative codes).
